instruction: I have a train record file on my desktop with train calling data. Each line shows: time, train_id, station_id, platform_no. I need to extract a list of all unique station IDs to understand which stations are covered. Can you help me create this list and save it at the end of the document?

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires extracting unique station IDs from train records. Verified with Python: 14 unique stations from 100 records. The evaluator extracts station_id (3rd field) from each line and checks against the expected sorted list of 14 unique stations.

llm_judge_reasons: Complete coverage: Evaluator verifies ALL instruction requirements - extraction of unique stations AND saving at end of document
Getter logic correctly identifies train records (4 comma-separated fields), finds the last record index, then searches only AFTER that point for station lists
The 'list_found_at_end' boolean ensures the list was actually saved at the end, not just extracted - returns False if no stations found after train records
Metric correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule' by directly accessing expected.get('stations'), not expected.get('rules')
Getter handles multiple output formats (comma-separated or one-per-line) and validates station format (3-letter uppercase codes)
Postconfig correctly saves document with Ctrl+S before evaluation, ensuring getter reads the modified file
Expected station list is semantically correct (14 unique stations: FAN, FTR, HHK, KOT, LMC, LOW, MOK, RAC, SHS, SHT, TAP, TAW, TWO, UNI)
Metric enforces both conditions for success: list_found_at_end==True AND stations match expected - returns 0.0 if either fails
Logic is robust with proper error handling for missing files, wrong types, and edge cases
